question: At fixed total expert/KV memory, do static layer budgets chosen on a disjoint calibration trace improve complete serving cost and old-request progress over uniform24?
hypothesis: Layer imbalance may leave a simple static budget improvement; compare minimizing calibration misses versus groups to expose their separate costs. This is a strong baseline, not a new predictor or novelty claim.

calibration.scope: 0_forward repeat0 none fixed routes, reset plus five warmups, faithful cap24 verification; no GPU counterfactual. Selection frozen before evaluation.

selection.rule: First three stored source-order documents disjoint from capacity-calibration documents; fixed 32/32/128 prefixes, not full-document serving.

workload.arrival: third request after both old requests have four output tokens
workload.policy: ordinary expert groups; chunk8 until both old complete, then release to global budget
workload.scope: Document-disjoint from capacity calibration; previously stored natural-text prefixes, not new source corpus or complete articles.

execution: Six fresh engines U/M/G/G/M/U, eight dependent episodes per engine. Each starts with own fixed layer caps and evolves all requests, KV, route, cache and completion independently. No online resize. All attempts retained.
primary: Complete capture wall with old max-ITL/completion and new TTFT/completion. Report full tradeoff; no outcome-selected SLO or scalar GO.
accounting: Also retain reset/five-warmup/raw-write/flush per-repeat cycles, post-init full engine cycles and parent process wall including init/shutdown. GC/CUDA spans overlap and are not subtracted. Calibration/qualification and tar/readback separately costed, never mixed into performance.
comparison: Two blocks of three engines, forward/reverse. All three policy pairs within each block at corresponding repeat ordinals are descriptive; aggregate eight repeats within each engine before presenting the two block effects. Neither repeated documents nor intraengine repeats create independent statistical samples.
qualification: Separate uniform/selected/min_groups 4-request expert execution with same-input full-expert numerical comparison at all16 layers. Finite and allclose(.01,.01), no bitwise/full-trajectory/quality claim. Qualification original input, not evaluation documents; excluded from performance.
conditions: Abort and retain incomplete requests, failed numerical qualification, source/resource mismatch or foreign GPU process/query failure. If request effects vary, retain every row and narrow model; do not retune layer allocation on evaluation results. Consistent better tradeoff warrants a further independent workload; no improvement here does not kill the research problem.
ceiling: One model/singleGPU/artificial expert pool, three document-disjoint evaluation prefixes, two engine blocks; no production SLO, population significance, generalized optimum or novel allocation claim.
cpu_checks: 16 existing adapter/grouping tests plus exact mapping/scratch/duplicate install checks passed; adapted phase reader exactly reproduces all old0_forward phases.
